worked_solution:
We use the identity $\operatorname{tan}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\operatorname{tan}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}\cdot \frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\int \operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x+C.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
